rinconraptor:study:1.title: Expanding the dinosaur diversity of the Cerro Overo–La Invernada area (Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Santonian), Northern Patagonia: Description of a new species and additional megaraptorid remains (Palaeontologia Electronica, 2026)

facts.statement: Rinconraptor is a newly named genus and species of megaraptorid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: A megaraptorid theropod. The type species is R. pipoae.

facts.statement: Rinconraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous Santonian age in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Rinconraptor () is an extinct genus of megaraptorid theropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian age) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Rinconraptor was described as a new genus and species by Ariel H. Méndez and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Ariel H. Méndez and colleagues described Rinconraptor pipoae as a new genus and species of megaraptoran dinosaur

facts.statement: Rinconraptor is estimated to have been about 7 metres long, placing it in the medium‑to‑large size range for megaraptorans.
facts.quote: Rinconraptor is regarded as a medium- to large-sized megaraptoran, with an estimated body length of 7 m.

facts.statement: Rinconraptor has a unique combination of humeral and tibial features, including a separated ectepicondyle, a straight lateral tibial margin, and a subrectangular cnemial crest and medial condyle.
facts.quote: Autapomorphies (unique derived features) of R. pipoae include the ectepicondyle being separated from the distal end of the humerus, the lateral (outer) margin of the tibia being straight when seen from above (proximal view), and the tibia's cnemial crest and medial condyle having a subrectangular shape.

facts.statement: Rinconraptor also possesses an anterodistally‑oriented ridge on the humerus and a right‑angled incisura tibialis, traits otherwise known only from Megaraptor and Fukuiraptor respectively.
facts.quote: It can further be distinguished from most other megaraptorans by having an anterodistally-oriented ridge on the humerus (a feature otherwise seen only in Megaraptor) and an incisura tibialis (a notch near the lateral condyle) that forms a right angle (only seen in Fukuiraptor).

facts.statement: The sediments of the Bajo de la Carpa Formation where Rinconraptor was found represent fluvial and aeolian systems in a semi‑arid paleoenvironment.
facts.quote: Its sediments represent fluvial and aeolian systems, with a semi-arid paleoenvironment.

facts.statement: Rinconraptor coexisted with other theropods such as the megaraptorid Tratayenia, abelisauroids Velocisaurus, Llukalkan and Viavenator, alvarezsaurids Achillesaurus and Alvarezsaurus, the unenlagiine Diuqin, and avialans Neuquenornis and Patagopteryx.
facts.quote: Theropods include the fellow megaraptorid Tratayenia, abelisauroids (Velocisaurus, Llukalkan, and Viavenator), alvarezsaurids (Achillesaurus and Alvarezsaurus), the unenlagiine paravian Diuqin, and the avialans (birds, in the broad sense) Neuquenornis and Patagopteryx.

facts.statement: Rinconraptor lived during the Santonian stage, approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only a single fossil occurrence of Rinconraptor has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
